column1: # BORU Language Specification: Function Application (apply)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# apply is the opposite-direction complement of `ref`: where `ref`/`/r`
# turns a call site into a Function VALUE, `apply` turns a Function value
# back into a CALL against the preceding stack arguments.
# apply is STACK-ONLY (it reads its function off the top of the stack):
#     <arg> ... <fn> apply
# so the canonical form pairs it with the `/r` suffix, which leaves the
# function on the stack without invoking:
#     5 inc/r apply        →  6        # inc applied to 5
# IMPORTANT — pair apply with the `/r` SUFFIX, not the `(ref …)` paren.
# A paren re-steps its contents, so `5 (ref inc) apply` fires `inc`
# against the stacked `5` FIRST (→ 6), leaving no function for `apply`.
# The `/r` suffix parks the function instead, which is what apply needs.
# §1  Basic application (args... fn/r apply)
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc/r apply
column3: apply a 1-arg referenced fn to one stack arg

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/r apply
column3: apply a 2-arg referenced fn (stack order: top→sig[0])

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  z/r apply
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc/r apply  add 100
column3: apply composes — its result stays on the stack

column1: # §2  apply on an anonymous-function reference
def f ([n:Integer] => [n add 1])  5 f/r apply
# §3  apply on a usurp (argument-reversed) wrapper
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/ur apply
column3: apply a reffed-usurp wrapper: args reversed (3 sub 10... reversed → 10 sub 3)

column1: # §4  Negatives
5 apply
column3: apply with no function on the stack

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc apply
column3: bare inc fires on 5 first (→6); apply then has no fn

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 (ref inc) apply
column3: (ref inc) paren re-steps inc on the stacked 5 — pair apply with /r, not (ref …)
